content: It is important to complete the full course of metronidazole treatment, even if your symptoms improve or resolve before finishing the medication. This helps reduce the risk of future infections becoming resistant to metronidazole or similar antibiotics. Uses of Vaginal Metronidazole: Vaginal metronidazole is an antibiotic commonly prescribed to treat bacterial vaginosis, an infection caused by specific bacteria. However, its effectiveness may vary depending on the bacteria causing the infection, as some bacteria in certain regions may have developed resistance to this medication. Vaginal metronidazole may also be used for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. Additionally, metronidazole is available in other forms, such as topical applications for the skin or oral and injectable formulations. Mechanism of Action: Vaginal metronidazole works by killing certain types of bacteria through damage to their DNA. Dosage Forms: Vaginal metronidazole is available as a 0.75% vaginal gel under brand names like Nuvessa, Vandazole, and generic formulations. It is inserted directly into the vagina. Storage Instructions: Store vaginal metronidazole at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). How to Use: The gel is inserted into the vagina as directed by your healthcare provider. Common Side Effects: The most common side effects of vaginal metronidazole include: Headache Vaginal itching Stomach pain Nausea Painful or heavy menstrual periods Sore throat Rash Diarrhea Breast pain (specific to Vandazole) Vaginal yeast infections (which may occur during or after treatment) Vaginal metronidazole does not treat yeast infections. If you experience symptoms of a yeast infection, such as vaginal discharge, itching, or discomfort, contact your healthcare provider. You may require treatment with an antifungal medication. If you experience any bothersome or unlisted side effects, consult your healthcare provider. Serious Side Effects: Although rare, serious side effects may occur. These include: Severe Allergic Reactions: Stop using vaginal metronidazole and seek immediate medical attention if you experience: Breathing difficulties or wheezing Rapid heartbeat Fever or general unwellness Swollen lymph nodes Swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat Difficulty swallowing or throat tightness Itching, skin rash, or hives Nausea or vomiting Dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting Stomach cramps Joint pain Nervous System Problems: Other forms of metronidazole (oral or injectable) have been associated with nervous system issues. Stop using vaginal metronidazole and contact your healthcare provider if you experience: Seizures Numbness, tingling, or pain in the hands or feet (peripheral neuropathy) Confusion, difficulty thinking, or behavioral changes Precautions: Who Should Not Use Vaginal Metronidazole: Do not use vaginal metronidazole if you are allergic to: Metronidazole Nuvessa Vandazole Parabens Other nitroimidazole derivatives Any ingredients in the specific product dispensed (your pharmacist can provide a full list of ingredients) Drug Interactions: Vaginal metronidazole should not be used with certain medications. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription, over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. Specific interactions include: Warfarin (Coumadin): Used to treat blood clots Disulfiram (Antabuse): Used to treat alcoholism (within the past 2 weeks) Lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid): Used to treat bipolar disorder Alcohol: Avoid consuming alcohol or foods containing alcohol or propylene glycol while using vaginal metronidazole and for at least 1 day after stopping Nuvessa or 3 days after stopping Vandazole. Combining alcohol with metronidazole can cause serious side effects. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Pregnancy: The effects of vaginal metronidazole on pregnancy or an unborn baby are not fully known. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. They will advise whether this medication is appropriate for you. Breastfeeding: Vaginal metronidazole passes into breast milk. If you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, discuss this with your healthcare provider. You may need to pump and discard your breast milk while using the medication and for 2 days after completing treatment. Overdose: If you or someone else uses too much vaginal metronidazole, seek immediate medical attention, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use double or extra doses. Completing the full prescribed course is essential, even if your symptoms improve, to prevent future infections from becoming resistant to metronidazole or similar medications. Important Notes: Do not use vaginal metronidazole unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. Use it exactly as directed and do not share it with others, even if they have the same condition. Keep it out of reach of children. Avoid sexual activity and the use of vaginal products like tampons or douches while using this medication. Vaginal metronidazole is for vaginal use only. If it comes into contact with your eyes, rinse them with cool water and contact your healthcare provider.
